title: P-256 negation-class rho v9b: complete doubled-add step pricing and bounded report routing

claims.statement: For the unrestricted-production P-256 challenge Q=[x]P, including the identity Q, the fully specified negation-class distinguished-point rho of argument.md recovers the canonical scalar with success at least 0.39, using total classical work at most 2^(3234/25) = 2^129.36 target-group-operation equivalents at the protected C=1000 scalar AArch64 instruction normalization. Architecture: negation classes {P,-P}, class key x, canonical member (x,|y|), doubling escape from the minimum-fingerprint class of the detected cycle, a 1.10 measured walk-quality allowance, N'=N*R/(R-1), a global work meter that halts at W_max, 64-bit distinguished points, and 2^16 storage nodes under a 16-bit routing field with per-node caps, charged set-up and routing inside H1. Step price: the transition canon(2X+T_j) is priced as the two batched affine additions X+(X+T_j) it actually is - core 4M+2S+12A = 1484, batch-inversion products 2 slots x 3M = 1320, batched Fermat inversion share 2, coefficient update 63, canonicalisation 14, degeneracy tests 12, itemised control 128, total 3023 instructions = 3.023 units, with M=220, S=176, A=21 itemised from four 64-bit limbs and no margin layered on the rows; this is 0.2521 bits cheaper than the published 3.6-unit single-addition allowance even after pricing both operations. Ledger: phase 1 3.023*(S_ops+2^60) = 2^129.24895 for S_ops = ceil(1.10*sqrt(2N'ln(1/0.60))) = 2^127.65297, reports 2^63.653 x 128 instructions = 2^60.687, setup 2^25.045, total 2^129.24895; every row repriced by 6/5 gives 2^129.51198. Escapes are arrivals: a doubling of at most 1620 instructions consumes one step slot priced at 3023, so no escape rate is assumed. Reports: the 64-bit DP condition gives expected 2^63.65297 reports <= 2^64 = a quarter of the 2^66-record, 2^72-byte capacity; Chernoff puts cap loss below 2^-8.8e19 and per node below 2^-100 after a 16-bit union bound, with cap-full reports refused and counted. Success: the meter leaves headroom 2^0.111 above the worst-case successful-trial cost, so the Markov halt debit is 2^-64.9 and the cap-loss debit is negligible; modelled success at S_ops is 1-0.60^1.21 = 0.4610 and 0.394-0.420 after the toy-measured walk efficiency 0.81-0.88, so the claim is 0.39. The bounded toy runs the production protocol end to end (DP endpoints, endpoint matching, exponent reconstruction, exact [x]P=Q verification, 16-bit routing to 2^16 nodes and to a 16-node capped pool): 0.3925 recovery on q26 at the production budget ratio against model 0.4309, 0.8325 at twice that budget against 0.8647, 0.3675 on the smaller q22 curve, zero mismatches, zero routing overflows, doubling escape trapping 5/150, 1/150, 0/150, 0/150 against additive escape 150/150. ord_r(2)=N is even, so the shortest sign-ambiguous doubling gap is N/2 = 2^253.99999999966 = 2^126.414*S_ops, correcting the published 2^127 phrasing. This is a supported exploratory analytic heuristic claim, not a theorem, a production run, a measured P-256 kernel price, an official score, novelty or a practical attack.
